events.title: Gary Kildall creates CP/M
events.summary: Gary Kildall created CP/M in 1974 — the first widely used disk operating system for microcomputers, running on Intel 8080 and Z80 machines.
events.about: CP/M gave early S-100 bus computers a standard command line, file system, and BIOS interface. IBM chose Microsoft's PC DOS over CP/M for the 1981 PC — but CP/M's design influenced DOS and proved micros needed real operating systems, not just monitor ROMs.

narrative.whyChosen: CP/M was the de facto OS for 8-bit microcomputers before the IBM PC.
narrative.whyImportant: It separated hardware BIOS from portable OS code — a model DOS and later systems copied.
narrative.problemSolved: Microcomputer owners needed disk file management and a consistent program environment.
